anti_patterns: Minting LRT against nominal token balance instead of DelegationManager share-balance: slashing leaves the token under-collateralized
Self-delegating the whole pool to one operator with uncapped AVS allocations: a single slash event haircuts every holder
Advertising instant redemption while the exit path needs undelegate plus withdrawal delay plus validator exit: users discover the queue during stress
Letting secondary-market price substitute for share-price accounting: depeg panic and donation/inflation manipulation go undetected
Auto-compounding arbitrary AVS reward tokens without review: worthless or malicious tokens inflate reported APY
Permissionless operator or AVS opt-in with no allowlist or allocation caps: novel slashing conditions enter the pool silently
avoid_when: Users need instant guaranteed redemption: exits pass through undelegate, withdrawal delay, and possibly validator exit
The team cannot underwrite AVS slashing conditions: each opted-in AVS adds a new slashable surface
Single-organization deployment with no DeFi composability need: a plain staking vault is simpler
Regulatory posture forbids pooled slashable derivatives or receipt-token lending collateral
Target chain has no mature restaking base layer with audited delegation and withdrawal contracts
benefits: Liquidity for locked restaking positions: ERC-20 LRT transfers instantly while underlying stake stays delegated
DeFi composability: LRT used as lending collateral, LP asset, or collateral in downstream protocols while still earning restaking yield
Delegation abstraction: depositors outsource operator selection, AVS underwriting, and reward claiming to the pool
Diversified AVS exposure: pooled capital spreads across operators and AVS operator sets with per-AVS allocation caps
Aggregated yield: beacon-chain rewards plus multiple AVS rewards compound into one exchange rate
Risk outsourcing option: holders choose a provider portfolio (conservative capped vs aggressive fully allocated) instead of managing slashing directly
best_practices: Mirror the DelegationManager share ledger on every state change: mint, burn, slash, and reward must reconcile shares not nominal balances
Curate operators with an allowlist and audit AllocationManager commitments so delegation matches advertised risk
Cap per-AVS allocation (e.g. conservative ceiling around 25%) to bound the blast radius of one slash event
Surface the full exit path in the UI: undelegate, withdrawal delay, validator exit for native ETH, and complete-as-tokens vs as-shares
Harvest RewardsCoordinator Merkle claims on a schedule, swap to the backing asset before reinvesting to keep single-asset backing
Protect share-price accounting against donation/inflation attacks with ERC-4626-style virtual shares or deposit minimums
Govern strategy upgrades, operator rotation, and fee changes behind timelock plus multisig or DAO vote
Monitor operator allocation changes continuously: delegated stake becomes slashable when operators opt into new operator sets
Seed and incentivize secondary-market liquidity so large holders can exit near backing value without waiting out the queue
component_types: Deposit Pool Vault: accepts ETH/LST deposits, mints and burns the LRT receipt token
LRT Token (ERC-20): fungible share receipt, reward-bearing or rebasing, tradable across DeFi
Config Registry: stores oracle, reward distributor, strategy, and operator-set addresses for modular upgrades
Delegation Router: assigns pooled shares to a curated operator set via the restaking base layer
Allocation Guard: enforces per-AVS and per-operator caps and allowlists on slashable commitments
Rewards Harvester: claims batched Merkle-distributed AVS rewards and compounds them into the pool
Withdrawal Queue: sequences undelegate, withdrawal delay, and completion as tokens or as shares
Exchange-Rate Oracle: publishes the LRT share price reflecting rewards minus slashing haircuts
context: Proof-of-stake capital restaked into additional validation duties (EigenLayer-style AVS security) earns extra yield but becomes illiquid: positions are delegated, slashable under each AVS slashing contract, and locked behind undelegate plus withdrawal-delay queues. Liquid Restaking Tokens wrap pooled restaking positions in a fungible ERC-20 so depositors keep transferability and DeFi composability while the vault handles delegation, AVS allocation, reward harvesting, slashing haircuts, and queued exits.
design_principles: Shares Not Tokens: the LRT mirrors the restaking share ledger, never the nominal deposit amount
Single Source of Truth: the restaking base layer owns balances, cooldowns, and slashing; the LRT reconciles, never bypasses
Bounded Blast Radius: per-AVS and per-operator allocation caps limit what one slash event can take
Transparent Queues: every exit path exposes undelegate, delay, and validator-exit steps honestly
Risk-Return Segmentation: conservative capped portfolios and aggressive fully allocated ones are distinct products

Curve / Balancer / Uniswap LRT liquidity pools
DeFi lending markets accepting LRT collateral
tradeoffs: Stacked slashing risk: every opted-in AVS adds independent slashing conditions on top of beacon-chain slashing
Depeg and liquidity risk: secondary-market LRT price can trade below backing value, and exits still need the full withdrawal queue (EigenLayer 7-day delay plus validator exit)
Operator concentration: pooled delegation to a curated set concentrates liveness and safety on few operators
Exchange-rate haircuts: slashing is socialized pro-rata across all LRT holders with no individual fault isolation
Reward complexity: AVS rewards arrive as batched Merkle claims in arbitrary tokens needing harvesting, swapping, and reinvestment
Governance trust: strategy upgrades, operator rotation, and fee changes depend on timelock/multisig discipline
Smart-contract surface: vault plus config plus token plus base-layer integrations multiply audit scope
use_cases: Restaking ETH or LSTs while keeping a liquid receipt token for DeFi use
Earning aggregated beacon plus AVS rewards through one reward-bearing token
Posting restaking exposure as collateral in lending markets without undelegating
Offering conservative vs aggressive AVS-allocation portfolios from one vault architecture
Rotating operators via complete-as-shares without exiting the underlying position
